abgox/pscompletions.first_step: Install the module from PowerShell Gallery on a personal workstation, run 'psc add git', and check whether it conflicts with your existing PSReadLine profile.
abgox/pscompletions.why: Shell tab-completion engine for PowerShell, bash, zsh and fish with a built-in completion library. It speeds up interactive CLI work but does not automate any admin task itself.

abhinavxd/libredesk.first_step: Run the Docker compose stack locally, connect a test mailbox, and trial it as an internal IT request inbox with SSO through a test OIDC app.
abhinavxd/libredesk.why: Self-hosted shared inbox and ticketing with email intake, knowledge base, SLAs, macros and OIDC SSO. It can serve as an internal IT helpdesk, though it is built for customer support and lacks ITSM asset features.

agentic-community/mcp-gateway-registry.first_step: Deploy it locally with Docker Compose and the bundled Keycloak, register one harmless read-only MCP server, and review the scopes and audit records before connecting your production IdP.
agentic-community/mcp-gateway-registry.why: Central gateway and registry for MCP servers and agents, with Entra ID/Okta/Keycloak OAuth, scoped access control, and audit logging. Useful for IT teams governing which agent tools staff can reach.

aixisstudio/snitch.first_step: Run it in demo mode (SNITCH_DEMO=1) or monitor-only on a test VM, and keep blocking rules and Lockdown Mode off until you have reviewed its alerts.
aixisstudio/snitch.why: Per-host outbound connection monitor and app firewall for macOS/Windows/Linux, with anomaly alerts, syslog/Wazuh SIEM export and a fleet agent. Useful for investigating suspicious traffic on individual endpoints.

ansible/ansible.first_step: Install ansible-core in a venv and run an ad-hoc read-only command (e.g., `ansible all -m ping` or gather facts) against a small test inventory.
ansible/ansible.why: Agentless SSH/WinRM configuration management for pushing config, packages and ad-hoc commands to servers and network gear. It is a general platform rather than a turnkey fix for identity or MDM tasks.

ansible/ansible-navigator.first_step: Install it with pip and run `ansible-navigator inventory -i inventory.yaml` or `ansible-navigator collections` to explore an existing setup without changing anything.
ansible/ansible-navigator.why: TUI and CLI for running Ansible playbooks, browsing inventories and collections, and running execution environments. Useful for sysadmins who already use Ansible for config management or network automation.

antonputra/tutorials.first_step: Browse docs/contents.md for a lesson matching your need, such as Terraform on AWS, and run its example in a sandbox cloud account.
antonputra/tutorials.why: Collection of DevOps tutorial code (Terraform, Kubernetes, Ansible, AWS/GCP) accompanying YouTube videos; useful as reference examples for cloud infrastructure, not for mainstream IT admin tasks.

aquasecurity/kube-bench.first_step: Apply the supplied job.yaml to a non-production cluster and review the pass/fail results in the pod logs.
aquasecurity/kube-bench.why: Runs CIS Kubernetes Benchmark checks against cluster nodes to produce hardening and compliance evidence. Useful to IT teams that run Kubernetes, which most identity, endpoint and SaaS admins do not.

aquasecurity/trivy.first_step: Install the binary and run `trivy fs --scanners vuln,secret,misconfig` against a non-production server directory or IaC repo to review findings locally.
aquasecurity/trivy.why: Scans container images, filesystems, VM images, Kubernetes clusters and IaC for CVEs, misconfigurations and exposed secrets. Useful for vulnerability management on servers and infrastructure, less so for endpoint/SaaS stacks.

art-of-wifi/unifi-api-browser.first_step: Deploy it on an internal PHP host that is not exposed to the internet, connect it to a test UniFi controller using a read-only admin account or API key, and browse the device and client lists.
art-of-wifi/unifi-api-browser.why: Web UI for browsing UniFi controller API data (devices, clients, firewall policies, VPN, events, stats) to troubleshoot UniFi networks and inspect data not shown in the controller UI.

art-of-wifi/unifi-api-client.first_step: Install via Composer and run a read-only call like listing devices or clients against a test site using a local admin or API key.
art-of-wifi/unifi-api-client.why: PHP client library for the UniFi Network Application API, useful for scripting device/client inventory, guest vouchers, stats and config on UniFi networks. Requires writing PHP code.

ascit31/dark-moon.first_step: Clone and run against an authorized sandbox target (e.g. OWASP Juice Shop) with a local model to review findings before any production use.
ascit31/dark-moon.why: Autonomous AI penetration testing across web, AD, cloud, K8s and CI/CD, runnable on a local LLM for self-hosted vulnerability assessment of your own infrastructure.

assafdori/bypass-mdm.first_step: Review it to understand the bypass vector and verify your MDM enforcement (Supervised/DEP) resists it, in a lab device.
assafdori/bypass-mdm.why: A script to bypass macOS MDM enrollment. Useful for sysadmins only as awareness of an evasion technique their fleet must defend against, not a management tool.

automatedlab/automatedlab.first_step: Install the module from PowerShell Gallery on an isolated Hyper-V host and run the single Windows 10 client sample script to validate the setup.
automatedlab/automatedlab.why: PowerShell framework to spin up Hyper-V or Azure test labs with AD, PKI, Exchange, SQL and ConfigMgr. Useful for testing GPOs, migrations and changes before production, but it does not manage production systems.

awesome-foss/awesome-sysadmin.first_step: Browse the HTML version's Identity Management, IT Asset Management, and Monitoring sections to shortlist tools worth evaluating.
awesome-foss/awesome-sysadmin.why: Curated index of open-source sysadmin software (backups, LDAP/SSO, asset management, monitoring, VPN) useful for finding self-hosted tools, but it is a list, not a tool.

badgerati/pode.first_step: Install the module from the PowerShell Gallery on a test machine and expose one read-only admin script (e.g., a status query) as a localhost-only GET route.
badgerati/pode.why: PowerShell web framework for wrapping existing admin scripts in REST APIs or small internal web tools, with Windows/Azure AD auth and cron-style scheduled tasks. It is a building block, not a ready-made admin tool.

batfish/batfish.first_step: Run the batfish/allinone Docker container, then load a snapshot of exported configs from a few devices and run the example notebooks. No device access is needed.
batfish/batfish.why: Validates firewall ACLs and router/switch configs (Cisco, Juniper, Palo Alto, Fortinet, AWS/Azure) offline, so you can check reachability and the impact of a change before deploying it.

beenuar/aisoc.first_step: Run `make up` on an isolated lab VM, load the synthetic sample data, and review AI triage verdicts before connecting any real tenant.
beenuar/aisoc.why: Self-hosted SOC platform that ingests EDR/SIEM/Okta telemetry, correlates alerts, and runs LLM triage with human-approved responses. Useful for small security teams, but heavy to deploy and operate.

bert-janp/hunting-queries-detection-rule.first_step: Copy a few Entra ID or Defender for Endpoint queries into Advanced Hunting and run them read-only to review the results before turning any into custom detection rules.
bert-janp/hunting-queries-detection-rule.why: Ready-made KQL hunting and detection queries for Defender for Endpoint, Defender XDR, Entra ID, Office 365 and Sentinel, useful for adding detection coverage and running incident response.

bestpractical/rt.first_step: Install RT on a test VM using SQLite and the standalone rt-server, then trial one helpdesk queue with email intake.
bestpractical/rt.why: Self-hosted open-source ticketing and asset tracking system for running an IT helpdesk queue and tracking work. It needs a Perl stack, a SQL database and a web server to deploy.

bijomaru78/eccm.first_step: Open the GitHub Pages demo and map one patch panel and switch, then export the layout as JSON to check it fits your documentation workflow.
bijomaru78/eccm.why: Browser-based tool for documenting physical Ethernet cabling: switches, patch panels and wall ports, with printable port and connection sheets. Useful for small-office or closet cable documentation.

bitwire-it/ipblocklist.first_step: Import outbound.txt as an external dynamic list on a test firewall in log-only mode, then review the hits for false positives before you enable blocking.
bitwire-it/ipblocklist.why: Aggregated inbound/outbound IP blocklists refreshed every 2 hours, consumable as external dynamic lists on pfSense, OPNsense, FortiGate, Palo Alto. Note: the data is CC BY-NC-SA, so commercial use is restricted.

bivlked/amneziawg-installer.first_step: Run the installer on a disposable Ubuntu 24.04 test VPS, then review the system changes it makes, including package removals and disabled unattended-upgrades.
bivlked/amneziawg-installer.why: One-command Bash installer for a self-hosted AmneziaWG (obfuscated WireGuard) VPN server on Ubuntu/Debian with client QR codes. It suits personal or anti-censorship use more than corporate remote access.

borgbase/vykar.first_step: Back up a non-critical test directory to a local or sandbox S3 repository, run it alongside your existing backup tool, and verify that restores work.
borgbase/vykar.why: Encrypted, deduplicated server and workstation backups to S3, SFTP or a REST server, with YAML config and built-in scheduling. The README says it is not yet ready for production backups.

bregman-arie/devops-exercises.first_step: Browse the Linux, Network and DNS topic sections to check your own knowledge or to draft interview questions for IT hires.
bregman-arie/devops-exercises.why: Interview questions and exercises covering Linux, networking, DNS, Ansible, Terraform and cloud; useful for skills study or for building hiring questions, not an operational tool.

bridgecrewio/checkov-action.first_step: Add the action to a test repository containing your Terraform with soft_fail: true and review the SARIF findings without blocking merges.
bridgecrewio/checkov-action.why: GitHub Action that runs Checkov to scan Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes and container images for misconfigurations; useful for IT teams managing infrastructure-as-code in GitHub repos.

bytedesk/bytedesk.first_step: Deploy the docker-compose stack on an isolated test VM and change the default admin/admin credentials immediately. Then evaluate the ticket and knowledge base modules, and review the BSL/AGPL licensing terms.
bytedesk/bytedesk.why: Self-hosted omnichannel customer-service platform with ticketing, SLA tracking and a knowledge base. It is aimed at external customer support more than internal IT service management, but could serve as an IT helpdesk.

capture0x/adstrike.first_step: Run in an isolated lab/sandbox AD domain with explicit authorization, starting with enumeration module 10 against a test DC.
capture0x/adstrike.why: Offensive AD red-team framework; useful for authorized pentesting/AD security validation, but it's an attack tool rather than a day-to-day sysadmin operations tool.

casdoor/casdoor.first_step: Run the casdoor-all-in-one Docker image locally with SQLite and wire one test app to it over OIDC before considering production use.
casdoor/casdoor.why: Self-hosted IdP providing SSO via OIDC, SAML, CAS, LDAP and SCIM with MFA, federating to Google Workspace and Entra ID. Useful for internal apps or labs, but it is an alternative IdP rather than a tool for managing Okta or Entra.

chainguard-dev/osquery-defense-kit.first_step: Install osquery on a test Mac or Linux host and run `make detect` to see which queries fire before loading any packs into production.
chainguard-dev/osquery-defense-kit.why: Ships 250+ osquery detection, policy and incident-response queries for macOS and Linux fleets, tuned to return zero rows normally so they can drive alerts in a SIEM or fleet manager.

chaitin/safeline.first_step: Deploy it in a lab VM in front of a non-production web app and review its detections in a monitoring-only posture before routing real traffic.
chaitin/safeline.why: Self-hosted WAF and reverse proxy that blocks SQLi, XSS, bots and brute force and rate-limits traffic in front of internal or public web apps. It is useful for protecting self-hosted tools, but it is not tied to the identity, endpoint or SaaS stack.

cisagov/scubagear.first_step: Install the module from PSGallery and run Invoke-SCuBA -ProductNames * with a read-only reviewer account against a test or production tenant, then review the HTML report.
cisagov/scubagear.why: PowerShell tool that audits an M365 tenant (Entra ID, Exchange, SharePoint, Teams, Defender, Power Platform) against CISA SCuBA baselines and outputs HTML/JSON/CSV reports usable as compliance evidence.

cloudposse/terraform-aws-s3-bucket.first_step: Run terraform plan with the module in a sandbox AWS account with user_enabled=false and review the planned bucket and policy resources.
cloudposse/terraform-aws-s3-bucket.why: Terraform module for provisioning AWS S3 buckets with encryption, lifecycle rules and public-access blocking. Cloud infrastructure building block more than core IT admin; useful for teams storing logs or backups in S3.

cmderdev/cmder.first_step: Extract the portable release to a user-writable folder on a workstation and try it as your daily shell before considering any shared install.
cmderdev/cmder.why: Portable Windows console emulator with tabbed cmd, PowerShell and Bash shells. It is a convenience for admins doing daily CLI work but does not administer any IT system itself.

codingwonders/dismtools.first_step: Install the portable build on a test VM and mount a copy of a Windows install.wim to inspect its packages and drivers without modifying production images.
codingwonders/dismtools.why: GUI front-end for DISM to service Windows WIM images: add drivers, features, and updates, build unattended answer files, and create test ISOs for OS deployment.

combodo/itop.first_step: Deploy it in a test VM or container, then import a sample CSV of assets to evaluate the CMDB and ticket workflows before connecting any production data sources.
combodo/itop.why: Self-hosted ITSM platform with a CMDB, ticketing, change and SLA management, and CSV import for tracking assets, incidents and service dependencies.

compasssecurity/entrafalcon.first_step: Run run_EntraFalcon.ps1 with a Global Reader account against a test or production tenant and review the Security Findings HTML report before changing anything.
compasssecurity/entrafalcon.why: Read-only PowerShell assessment of Entra ID that flags privileged objects, risky app permissions, users without MFA, Conditional Access gaps and PIM assignments, with output as HTML reports.

crossplane/crossplane.first_step: Install Crossplane into a local kind cluster and follow the get-started composition quickstart against a sandbox cloud account.
crossplane/crossplane.why: Kubernetes-based control plane for declaratively managing cloud infrastructure; relevant to platform/cloud engineers more than identity, endpoint or SaaS admins.

crowdstrike/falconpy.first_step: Create a Falcon API client with read-only scopes (e.g. Hosts: Read) and use the Hosts service class to list devices in a test CID.
crowdstrike/falconpy.why: Official Python SDK for the CrowdStrike Falcon API, used to script host inventory, detections, containment, policy and sensor management without hand-rolling OAuth2 token handling.

cyb3rmik3/kql-threat-hunting-queries.first_step: Copy a single query into Defender XDR Advanced Hunting, run it read-only over a short time range, and review the results before turning it into a detection rule.
cyb3rmik3/kql-threat-hunting-queries.why: Collection of KQL hunting and detection queries for Microsoft Sentinel and Defender XDR, useful for M365 security teams writing hunts or analytics rules. Currently being rebuilt, so content may be in flux.

cyb3rxp/awesome-soc.first_step: Skim the Playbooks/SOP and incident response sections to compare against your own IR runbooks.
cyb3rxp/awesome-soc.why: Curated reading list on building and running a SOC/CSIRT: detection engineering, IR playbooks, SOC metrics. Useful as background for sysadmins who share security duties, but it is links, not tooling.

datacleaner/datacleaner.first_step: Load a CSV export of user or asset records into the desktop app and run a profiling job to spot duplicates and missing fields.
datacleaner/datacleaner.why: General data quality and profiling desktop tool. Sysadmins could use it to profile and deduplicate exported directory or asset inventory data, but it is not IT-admin specific.

dataplat/dbatools.first_step: Install it for the current user and run read-only commands like Get-DbaLastBackup and Get-DbaDatabase against a non-production instance.
dataplat/dbatools.why: PowerShell module with ~700 commands for SQL Server administration: backup verification, instance migration, finding databases across servers, and health checks. Most useful where IT also looks after SQL Server.

deepfence/threatmapper.first_step: Deploy the Management Console with docker-compose in a lab and run an agentless Cloud Scanner against a non-production AWS, Azure or GCP account before installing the privileged sensor agents.
deepfence/threatmapper.why: Open-source CNAPP that scans hosts, containers and Kubernetes for vulnerabilities, exposed secrets and cloud misconfigurations against compliance benchmarks. Most useful for teams that run their own cloud or container infrastructure.

defectdojo/django-defectdojo.first_step: Run it locally with docker compose and import a sample scan report from your existing vulnerability scanner to evaluate deduplication and reporting.
defectdojo/django-defectdojo.why: Self-hosted vulnerability management platform that imports scanner output, deduplicates findings and tracks remediation. Useful for IT security teams consolidating scan results, though it is oriented toward AppSec/DevSecOps.

deploymenttheory/terraform-provider-jamf.first_step: Point the provider at a non-production Jamf Pro instance with a limited-scope OAuth2 API client, import a few existing objects, and run terraform plan to review drift without applying.
deploymenttheory/terraform-provider-jamf.why: Terraform provider that manages Jamf Pro configuration (policies, groups, profiles, apps) as code, enabling version control, change review, drift detection and replication across tenants.

dirkjanm/roadtools.first_step: Run roadrecon against your tenant with read-only Graph credentials to dump data to a local DB and explore in the GUI.
dirkjanm/roadtools.why: Dumps and explores all Entra ID/Azure AD data into a queryable offline database for security review and access analysis; useful for blue-team audits of tenant configuration.

django-crm/django-crm.first_step: Run the docker compose quick start locally with demo data and review the helpdesk module to judge whether it could handle internal IT tickets.
django-crm/django-crm.why: Self-hosted sales CRM that includes a helpdesk module with SLA timers, escalations and a knowledge base. It is customer-facing, not internal IT service management, so its use for IT ticketing is limited.

django-helpdesk/django-helpdesk.first_step: Run the docker compose demo locally, create a test queue, and evaluate the ticket workflow before considering production use.
django-helpdesk/django-helpdesk.why: Self-hosted Django ticket tracker for running a small internal helpdesk with queues and ticket tracking. It needs hosting and setup, and has no mainstream identity or MDM integrations documented.

docker-mailserver/docker-mailserver.first_step: Deploy the container in an isolated lab with a test domain, following the basic-installation tutorial, and verify DKIM/DMARC and spam filtering before any production use.
docker-mailserver/docker-mailserver.why: Self-hosted containerized mail server (Postfix, Dovecot, Rspamd, ClamAV, DKIM/DMARC) for running on-prem email or relay without Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace. Also usable for internal SMTP relays or test mail environments.

dotnet/dev-proxy.first_step: Install it on a dev workstation and run the microsoft-graph-rate-limiting preset while executing an existing read-only Graph script against a test tenant.
dotnet/dev-proxy.why: Developer tool that intercepts HTTP calls to simulate API errors and throttling, including Microsoft Graph rate limits. It can help test whether internal Graph automation scripts handle 429s and retries.

drduh/macos-security-and-privacy-guide.first_step: Read the FileVault, firewall and Gatekeeper sections and compare them against your current Jamf/Intune macOS profiles, using the NIST macOS Security Compliance Project for fleet-ready baselines.
drduh/macos-security-and-privacy-guide.why: Hardening reference for macOS covering FileVault, firewall/pf, Gatekeeper, SIP and logging; useful for drafting Mac security baselines, though aimed at individual users rather than MDM-managed fleets.

dromara/maxkey.first_step: Deploy the Docker build in an isolated lab, connect it to a test LDAP/AD, and federate one non-production SAML or OIDC app.
dromara/maxkey.why: Self-hosted open-source IdP providing SSO (SAML, OIDC, CAS), MFA, SCIM provisioning and AD/LDAP account management. An alternative to Okta/Entra, but it requires running and maintaining a Java/MySQL stack.

ediwang/moonglade.first_step: Not applicable for IT administration; if you are curious, run it locally with docker compose to evaluate it as a blog.
ediwang/moonglade.why: A self-hosted personal blog platform in ASP.NET Core. It supports Entra ID/OIDC sign-in, but it does not automate or improve any IT administration task.

ehmo/gum.first_step: Install it, authorize a test Workspace account with narrow scopes via your own Desktop OAuth client, and run only `gum read` operations such as listing users or messages.
ehmo/gum.why: CLI and MCP server for calling Google Workspace APIs (Admin, Gmail, Drive, Vault, Calendar), with read/write/destructive separation and confirmation gates. Useful for scripting or agent-assisted Workspace admin queries.

emersonfelipesp/netbox-proxbox.first_step: Install the plugin on a non-production NetBox instance, leave the endpoint's allow_writes gate off, and run an on-demand sync against a test Proxmox cluster using a read-only API token.
emersonfelipesp/netbox-proxbox.why: Syncs Proxmox clusters, nodes, VMs, containers, backups and IPs into NetBox so the inventory and source of truth match what is actually running. Useful for shops running both Proxmox and NetBox.

enms-automation/enms.first_step: Deploy the open core in an isolated lab VM and run config backups against a few test devices using read-only credentials.
enms-automation/enms.why: Network automation platform for device config backup with Git diffs, Netmiko/NAPALM validation, and scheduled Ansible/Python workflows. Useful for network teams, but the open core lacks auth and RBAC.

ep1cman/unifi-protect-backup.first_step: Run the Docker container with a dedicated local Protect account, backing up to a local /data volume with a short retention, and confirm that clips are captured before you add a cloud rclone remote.
ep1cman/unifi-protect-backup.why: Backs up UniFi Protect camera event clips in real time to off-site storage via rclone, with retention pruning. Useful for IT teams that run UniFi physical security cameras.

evotecit/eventviewerx.first_step: Install PSEventViewer from the PowerShell Gallery on an admin workstation and run a read-only failed-logon or lockout query against one domain controller.
evotecit/eventviewerx.why: PowerShell module for querying Windows event logs across hosts, with built-in reports for AD lockouts, failed logons, group changes and Kerberos failures, WEC management, and export to CSV/HTML/Excel.

fatedier/frp.first_step: Run frps on a lab VPS with token or OIDC auth and an allowPorts restriction, then tunnel a single test SSH service from a sandbox machine.
fatedier/frp.why: Self-hosted reverse proxy and tunnel for exposing internal services (SSH, RDP, web apps) behind NAT or firewalls. Useful for remote access to lab or branch systems, but it bypasses perimeter controls, so it needs security review.

faveosuite/faveo-helpdesk.first_step: Deploy the community edition in a test VM with MySQL, disable Bugsnag error reporting, and trial an internal IT ticket queue with email intake.
faveosuite/faveo-helpdesk.why: Self-hosted open source ticketing system (Laravel/PHP) that IT teams could run as an internal helpdesk; it is customer-support oriented, and the community edition lacks asset management.

fleetdm/fleet.first_step: Stand up a trial Fleet server and enroll a few test machines with the osquery agent to review inventory and CIS policy results before enabling MDM or software deployment.
fleetdm/fleet.why: Open-source MDM and osquery-based device management for macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS and Android: inventory, software deployment and patching, CIS benchmark checks, and GitOps-managed config.

fortinetdev/terraform-provider-fortios.first_step: Point the provider at a lab or non-production FortiGate with a limited-scope API token and run terraform plan against imported data sources to see the diff before applying anything.
fortinetdev/terraform-provider-fortios.why: Official Fortinet Terraform provider for managing FortiGate (FortiOS 6.0–7.6) firewall policies, addresses, VPNs and interfaces as code, replacing manual GUI changes.

frappe/helpdesk.first_step: Run the Docker development setup locally, change the default admin password, and trial a few internal IT ticket workflows and KB articles before planning a production deployment.
frappe/helpdesk.why: Self-hosted open-source ticketing system with SLAs, assignment rules, saved replies and a knowledge base; usable as an internal IT helpdesk, though it is built for customer support.

freescout-help-desk/freescout.first_step: Try the public demo, then deploy the Docker image on a test VM connected to a non-production shared mailbox to evaluate ticket intake.
freescout-help-desk/freescout.why: Self-hosted shared mailbox and ticketing system that can serve as an internal IT helpdesk queue, with OAuth mailbox connections for Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace. It is customer-support oriented, with no built-in asset management or ITSM workflows.

future-architect/vuls.first_step: Run a non-root fast scan over SSH against a single non-production Linux server and review the report in the TUI viewer.
future-architect/vuls.why: Agentless SSH-based vulnerability scanning of Linux/FreeBSD servers, containers, and some Windows/macOS, matching packages against NVD, OVAL, and KEV. Reports by cron with Slack or email alerts.

glpi-project/glpi.first_step: Deploy it in a test VM with MariaDB, inventory a few machines with GLPI Agent, and walk a sample ticket through the workflow before importing production data.
glpi-project/glpi.why: Self-hosted ITSM and asset management: ticketing, CMDB, agent-based hardware/software inventory, license tracking, contracts and a knowledge base.

google/mcp-security.first_step: Install the GTI or SecOps MCP server with uvx and connect it to Claude Desktop using credentials scoped to read-only viewer roles in a non-production project.
google/mcp-security.why: MCP servers that let an AI client query Google SecOps (Chronicle) SIEM, SOAR cases, Google Threat Intelligence and Security Command Center for alert triage and threat hunting. Useful only if you run Google's security stack.

google/osv-scanner.first_step: Run `osv-scanner scan source -r` against a repo of internal admin scripts or tools, or `osv-scanner scan image` against an existing container image, and review the report.
google/osv-scanner.why: Scans source dependencies, container images and Linux OS packages for known vulnerabilities using OSV.dev. Useful for vulnerability checks on internal scripts, tools and server images, but it targets developer dependencies more than managed endpoints.

google/osv.dev.first_step: Query the public OSV API at osv.dev for a package version your team runs instead of deploying this GCP codebase.
google/osv.dev.why: Source for the osv.dev open source vulnerability database and API, focused on software dependency vulnerabilities. Useful to IT mainly as a data source for vulnerability lookups, not endpoint or fleet patching.

googleworkspace/apps-script-oauth2.first_step: Add the library to a test Apps Script project and authorize against a sandbox API to confirm token storage and refresh behavior.
googleworkspace/apps-script-oauth2.why: Apps Script library that handles OAuth2 token flows and refresh. Useful as a building block when Google Workspace admin scripts need to call third-party APIs such as Okta or Slack.

googleworkspace/apps-script-samples.first_step: Copy the adminSDK sample into an Apps Script project in a test Workspace domain and run its read-only list functions, such as listing users, before adapting it.
googleworkspace/apps-script-samples.why: Official Google Apps Script samples, including Admin SDK directory and domain management, Drive activity, and Gmail examples, that Workspace admins can adapt into scripts for user, group and Drive tasks.

googleworkspace/cli.first_step: Install gws against a test Workspace tenant. Log in with narrow read-only scopes, run list commands such as admin directory users list, and use --dry-run before any write call.
googleworkspace/cli.why: A CLI built from Google's Discovery Service that covers every Workspace API, Admin included. Use it to script user, group, Drive and Gmail admin tasks with JSON output, and it ships agent skills for LLM-driven management.

googleworkspace/google-chat-samples.first_step: Deploy the Webhook app sample to post a test message into a test Chat space in a non-production Workspace tenant.
googleworkspace/google-chat-samples.why: Developer samples for building Google Chat apps and bots. Useful as a starting point for IT teams building helpdesk bots or webhook alerts into Google Chat, but they are not admin tooling.

googleworkspace/node-samples.first_step: Clone the repo and run a read-only Drive or Admin SDK sample against a test Workspace tenant using a service account with minimal scopes.
googleworkspace/node-samples.why: Official Node.js code samples for Google Workspace APIs (Drive, Slides, etc.), useful as reference snippets when writing custom Workspace admin scripts.

googleworkspace/python-samples.first_step: Run the Admin SDK Directory quickstart with read-only scopes against a test Workspace domain to list users.
googleworkspace/python-samples.why: Official Python quickstart samples for Google Workspace APIs, including Admin SDK Directory and Reports. Useful as starting code for scripting user listings or audit log pulls, but not a finished tool.

greenbone/openvas-scanner.first_step: Deploy the Greenbone Community Containers in a lab VM and run an authorized scan against a single test host on an isolated subnet.
greenbone/openvas-scanner.why: The OpenVAS scan engine behind Greenbone Community Edition, used for network vulnerability scanning of hosts. It is only one component, so you need the full GVM stack or the community containers around it.

grokability/snipe-it.first_step: Try the hosted live demo, or run the Docker image locally with test data, before syncing any real Jamf or Kandji inventory.
grokability/snipe-it.why: Self-hosted IT asset and license management for tracking who has which laptop, purchase and depreciation data, and software licenses. It has a REST API and integrations such as jamf2snipe and Kandji2Snipe.

guacsec/guac.first_step: Bring up the docker compose quickstart with the in-memory keyvalue backend and ingest a few sample SBOMs to test vulnerability queries.
guacsec/guac.why: Aggregates SBOMs, VEX, OSV and SLSA attestations into a queryable graph for software supply chain vulnerability and dependency analysis. Mostly AppSec/DevSecOps territory rather than day-to-day IT admin work.

h-mdm/hmdm-server.first_step: Install the web panel on a test Ubuntu VM and enroll one factory-reset spare Android device via QR code to evaluate app deployment and configs.
h-mdm/hmdm-server.why: Self-hosted open-source Android MDM: QR enrollment, app deployment, device groups and configuration. Useful for Android fleets or kiosks outside Intune, but key lockdown features are in the paid edition.

hairyhenderson/gomplate.first_step: Install the binary and render a sample config file from a local YAML datasource to see whether it fits your existing config-generation scripts.
hairyhenderson/gomplate.why: General-purpose CLI template renderer that builds config files from env vars, YAML/JSON, Vault or Consul. Handy for generating configs in scripts, but it does not target any IT admin platform.

harmveenstra/powershellisfun.first_step: Pick a read-only reporting script, such as the M365 license overview or AD OU permissions report, read its blog post, and run it against a test tenant or lab domain.
harmveenstra/powershellisfun.why: Collection of blog-backed PowerShell scripts for Intune printer/WinGet deployment, AD permission reports, Exchange permission copying, M365 license reports and MFA setup. Each needs per-script review and adaptation.

hashicorp/terraform.first_step: Install the CLI, write a small config using a provider such as Okta or Entra ID against a sandbox tenant, and run only 'terraform plan' to review the proposed changes without applying them.
hashicorp/terraform.why: Terraform core is the IaC engine behind providers for Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace and cloud networks, letting admins version and review tenant and infrastructure config. It needs separate providers and workflow setup to be useful.

hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm.first_step: Write a small config for a test resource group in a sandbox subscription and run terraform plan only, to review the proposed changes without applying them.
hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm.why: Official Terraform provider for managing Azure infrastructure as code, such as resource groups, virtual networks and VMs. It is useful for teams running Azure infrastructure, though it is cloud-infra focused rather than Entra/Intune admin.

helpcode-ai/anythingmcp.first_step: Run the localhost quickstart in Docker and connect a single test API whose credentials allow read-only access only. Then check the per-tool permissions and the audit log.
helpcode-ai/anythingmcp.why: Self-hosted MCP gateway that exposes REST, SOAP, SQL and file shares to AI clients with RBAC and audit logs. Its connectors focus on ERP and e-commerce, so for IT admins it is mainly a platform for building agents, not a sysadmin tool.

holo-routing/holo.first_step: Try a topology in the browser-based Holo Lab, or deploy a prebuilt containerlab topology in an isolated lab before going near production routing.
holo-routing/holo.why: Rust routing protocol suite (OSPF, BGP, IS-IS, BFD, VRRP) with YANG/gNMI management. It suits network engineers building Linux software routers or labs, and is of limited use for typical corporate IT administration.

hotcakex/harden-windows-security.first_step: Install Harden System Security on a test VM and run its compliance check to compare current settings against its baseline before applying any changes.
hotcakex/harden-windows-security.why: Hardens Windows using Microsoft-supported settings (Defender, BitLocker, firewall, WDAC). AppControl Manager helps build and deploy App Control for Business policies. Useful for baseline and application-allowlisting work.

iainkay/ram-altman.first_step: If curious, run ./ram-altman.sh --status or --dry-run on a personal Linux box to read the memory figures without sending any email.
iainkay/ram-altman.why: A parody bash script that emails a daily joke about unused RAM. Its /proc/meminfo accounting is correct, but it is not a practical memory monitoring tool for IT work.

infobyte/faraday.first_step: Run the docker-compose stack locally and import an existing Nmap or scanner XML report with faraday-cli into a test workspace.
infobyte/faraday.why: Self-hosted vulnerability manager that imports and normalizes output from 80+ scanners (Nmap, Burp, ZAP, etc.) into shared workspaces for tracking remediation. It suits security-focused IT teams more than general admin work.

jaegeral/security-apis.first_step: Browse the list for a free, no-auth API such as CIRCL CVE Search or hashlookup and test a single query from a script.
jaegeral/security-apis.why: Curated list of public security APIs (threat intel, CVE feeds, IP/domain reputation, sandboxes) that can serve as data sources for enrichment scripts or SIEM integrations.

jamf-concepts/mcp-hub.first_step: Connect it to a Jamf Pro sandbox instance using an API client limited to read privileges, and run inventory queries such as listing computers by macOS version.
jamf-concepts/mcp-hub.why: MCP server from Jamf with 50 tools for querying and managing Jamf Pro devices, smart groups, policies and profiles, plus Jamf Protect alerts and Security Cloud risk status.

jkroepke/openvpn-auth-oauth2.first_step: Run the Docker Compose demo against a test app registration in a sandbox IdP tenant before touching a production OpenVPN server.
jkroepke/openvpn-auth-oauth2.why: Adds OIDC SSO to OpenVPN servers using Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace or Keycloak, replacing static VPN credentials with your IdP login and MFA policies.

jm33-m0/emp3r0r.first_step: Not applicable for defensive sysadmin use.
jm33-m0/emp3r0r.why: This is an offensive C2/post-exploitation and malware framework for red teaming, not a tool for administering identity, endpoints, SaaS, or networks.

jmpsec/osctrl.first_step: Deploy osctrl in a lab with a few test hosts enrolled, run saved read-only queries, and connect osctrl-mcp with mutating tools left disabled.
jmpsec/osctrl.why: Self-hosted osquery fleet manager for running distributed queries across endpoints, carving files, alerting on node state, and tracking posture mapped to SOC 2/ISO 27001. Includes an MCP server for fleet inspection.

kanidm/kanidm.first_step: Deploy a test instance in a container per the Kanidm book, then connect one non-critical app via OIDC or one Linux host via the unix client.
kanidm/kanidm.why: Self-hosted identity provider with OIDC SSO, passkeys, RADIUS for VPN/Wi-Fi, SSH key distribution and Linux login. An alternative to FreeIPA/Keycloak, not a tool for managing Okta or Entra ID.

karib0u/rustinel.first_step: Run it on a lab VM with the demo rule, then capture a session and replay it against a rules pack to see which alerts fire before deploying anywhere.
karib0u/rustinel.why: Open-source endpoint detection agent that runs Sigma, YARA and IOC rules on Windows/Linux/macOS telemetry and writes ECS alerts for Splunk or Elastic. It is useful for detection testing or supplementing EDR, but it is not a managed EDR replacement.

kchristensen/udm-le.first_step: Check whether your UniFi OS version already offers built-in Let's Encrypt under Control Plane > Console before installing this; if you still need it, test on a lab device with Let's Encrypt staging.
kchristensen/udm-le.why: Shell script that issues and renews Let's Encrypt certificates on UniFi OS gateways via DNS-01 using Lego. The author says it is mostly obsolete now that UniFi OS 5.1 has this built in.

kdeldycke/awesome-iam.first_step: Skim the MFA, password-less and SAML sections for references relevant to your Okta or Entra ID rollout plans.
kdeldycke/awesome-iam.why: Curated reading list on IAM concepts (SSO, MFA, SAML, SCIM, passkeys, zero trust). It's aimed mostly at developers building auth, but useful background for admins designing identity policy.

kesslernity/awesome-copilot-studio-agent.first_step: Paste one instruction-only agent into Agent Builder in a test tenant with a Copilot licence, and check how it behaves before sharing it with users.
kesslernity/awesome-copilot-studio-agent.why: A library of prompt instruction blocks for M365 Copilot declarative agents, mostly aimed at business users (writing, PM, HR). M365 admins rolling out Copilot could use it as starter content for users.

lacs-project/sysknife.first_step: Install on a disposable Ubuntu VM and use only the read-only query tools and sysknife_plan, without approving any execution receipts.
lacs-project/sysknife.why: MCP server that lets an AI assistant administer Ubuntu/Fedora Atomic hosts through typed, human-approved actions (apt, ufw, systemd) with a signed audit log. Useful for Linux server ops, not mainstream SaaS/MDM stacks.

lazywinadmin/powershell.first_step: Browse the repo for a read-only AD or O365 reporting function, review its code, and run it in a test domain or tenant.
lazywinadmin/powershell.why: A collection of PowerShell functions for Active Directory, SCCM, Exchange/O365, Azure and VMware admin tasks. It is useful as a script library, but each script needs review and adaptation before use.

lefayjey/linwinpwn.first_step: Run in automated enumeration-only mode against a lab/sandbox domain controller with authorized credentials.
lefayjey/linwinpwn.why: Offensive AD pentesting wrapper (BloodHound, impacket, kerberoast, certipy). Sysadmins can use it to audit their own AD for weaknesses like ZeroLogon, noPac, ASREPRoast and ADCS misconfigs.

lemker/unifi-os-server.first_step: Deploy the docker-compose file on a test host, then adopt a single spare UniFi device via set-inform before migrating any production sites.
lemker/unifi-os-server.why: Packages Ubiquiti's UniFi OS Server as a container for Docker, Kubernetes or Home Assistant, so you can self-host the UniFi controller for device adoption and multi-site network management.

lethal-forensics/microsoft-analyzer-suit.first_step: Export sign-in and audit logs from a test tenant with Microsoft-Extractor-Suite, then run the matching analyzer offline against those files and review the output.
lethal-forensics/microsoft-analyzer-suit.why: Analyzes Entra ID sign-in/audit logs, M365 Unified Audit Log, MFA status, OAuth grants, mailbox permissions and transport rules exported by Microsoft-Extractor-Suite, for incident response and tenant review.

lissy93/networking-toolbox.first_step: Run the Docker image locally with `docker run -p 3000:3000 lissy93/networking-toolbox` and try the subnet and DNS tools against known values.
lissy93/networking-toolbox.why: Self-hosted web toolbox of 100+ networking utilities (subnet/CIDR calculators, converters, DNS and config diagnostics) for day-to-day network troubleshooting and planning.

lissy93/web-check.first_step: Run the Docker image locally with `docker run -p 3000:3000 lissy93/web-check` and scan one of your own public domains.
lissy93/web-check.why: Self-hosted web app that inspects a domain's DNS, TLS certificates, security headers, open ports and mail config. Useful for auditing your organization's public-facing sites and email domains.

lkarlslund/adalanche.first_step: Run the collector with a standard read-only domain user against a lab or test domain, then review the attack paths in the local web UI before running it in production.
lkarlslund/adalanche.why: Collects Active Directory ACLs, group memberships and Windows machine data to graph who can effectively reach Domain Admin. It also flags delegation errors, kerberoastable accounts and AD CS misconfigurations.

m14r41/pentestingeverything.first_step: Browse the Configuration Review and Network Pentesting sections on the website to compare against your own hardening checklist, without installing the agent skill.
m14r41/pentestingeverything.why: A pentesting knowledge base and checklists covering network, Wi-Fi, AD, cloud, and configuration review. Useful as reference when hardening infrastructure or preparing for an external assessment, but it does not automate admin tasks.

macadmins/nudge.first_step: Deploy Nudge with a test configuration profile to a small pilot group of Macs via your MDM and check the deferral prompts and deadlines.
macadmins/nudge.why: Prompts Mac users to install required macOS updates with configurable deferrals and deadlines, using the SOFA feed to track current releases. Deploy it via Jamf or Intune.

macjutsu/super.first_step: Deploy the stable 5.1.x release to a small test group of Macs through Jamf Pro and review the update dialogs and deferral behavior before rolling it out more widely.
macjutsu/super.why: Enforces macOS and Apple software updates with user dialogs, deferrals, deadlines, and restarts, and can run Jamf Pro policies. Covers a recurring Mac patch-compliance task.

maester365/maester.first_step: Install the release build (2.3.0 or current stable) in PowerShell 7.4, run Connect-Maester and Invoke-Maester against a test tenant, and review the HTML report.
maester365/maester.why: PowerShell framework that runs automated security configuration checks against Entra ID and Microsoft 365 tenants (Conditional Access, Exchange, etc.) and reports drift, with CI/CD and Teams/email notifications.

mdecrevoisier/evtx-to-mitre-attack.first_step: Load a handful of the EVTX samples into a non-production SIEM index or a local tool like Zircolite and check which of your existing detections trigger.
mdecrevoisier/evtx-to-mitre-attack.why: Provides over 270 Windows/AD/Sysmon EVTX attack samples mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, for testing whether your SIEM detection rules fire on AD, Defender and Exchange events.

mhsanaei/3x-ui.first_step: Install it on a disposable test VPS to evaluate the panel and API. Do not expose it on corporate networks, since the README states it is not intended for production.
mhsanaei/3x-ui.why: Web panel for running Xray-core proxy/VPN servers (VLESS, Trojan, WireGuard) with per-client quotas. It is aimed at censorship circumvention and personal use, not corporate VPN or remote-access administration.

michaelcade/90daysofdevops.first_step: Read the 2022 DevOps track sections on Ansible and Terraform and work through the labs in a personal lab environment.
michaelcade/90daysofdevops.why: A free learning curriculum covering DevOps basics like Linux, networking, Terraform, Ansible and containers. Useful for sysadmins building automation skills, but it is training material rather than an admin tool.

michaelgrafnetter/dsinternals.first_step: Install from PowerShell Gallery in a lab, then run Test-PasswordQuality against an offline ntds.dit copy from a test domain, with security team approval since it can dump hashes.
michaelgrafnetter/dsinternals.why: PowerShell module for Active Directory password auditing (shared and breached passwords via Test-PasswordQuality), key credential audits, LAPS and BitLocker key recovery, and DC recovery from IFM backups.

micke-k/intunemanagement.first_step: Run a bulk export with read-only Graph permissions against a test tenant and review the generated JSON and documentation before trying any import.
micke-k/intunemanagement.why: Exports, backs up, documents, compares and migrates Intune policies and profiles, including assignments, between tenants via Graph, with a UI or silent batch mode.

micromdm/micromdm.first_step: Follow the ngrok demo guide to stand up a test instance and enroll a spare test Mac, or evaluate NanoMDM instead given v1's end of support.
micromdm/micromdm.why: Open-source API-driven Apple MDM server for enrolling Macs/iOS devices via DEP and pushing commands, but v1 is in maintenance mode with support ending 2025; NanoMDM is the successor.

microsoft/mcp.first_step: Install the Azure MCP Server locally and point it at a sandbox subscription with a Reader-only role to test resource queries.
microsoft/mcp.why: Hosts the official Azure MCP Server and catalogs Microsoft MCP servers, letting agents query Azure resources. Useful for cloud infra admins, less so for identity, endpoint or M365 administration.

microsoft/shell-intune-samples.first_step: Pick one macOS custom attribute or config script, review it, and deploy it via Intune to a single test Mac in a pilot group.
microsoft/shell-intune-samples.why: Microsoft-maintained shell script samples for Intune-managed macOS and Linux: app installs, device config, custom attributes and Linux custom compliance checks.

microsoft365dsc/microsoft365dsc.first_step: Install the module and export a snapshot of a test tenant's configuration with read-only credentials, then review it before applying anything.
microsoft365dsc/microsoft365dsc.why: Exports, deploys and monitors Microsoft 365 tenant configuration (Entra ID, Exchange, Intune, Teams, SharePoint, Defender) as PowerShell DSC code, so you can back it up and catch configuration drift.

microsoftdocs/powershell-docs.first_step: Browse the reference folder for your PowerShell version, or run Update-Help locally to get the same content offline.
microsoftdocs/powershell-docs.why: Source for the official PowerShell cmdlet reference and conceptual docs. It is useful as a reference while writing admin scripts, but it is documentation, not a tool.

microsoftgraph/msgraph-sdk-javascript.first_step: Register an app in a test tenant with read-only Graph permissions like User.Read.All and write a small Node script that lists users.
microsoftgraph/msgraph-sdk-javascript.why: Official JavaScript/TypeScript SDK for Microsoft Graph, a building block for custom scripts that query or manage Entra ID users, groups, and Microsoft 365 data such as mail and OneDrive.

microsoftgraph/msgraph-sdk-powershell.first_step: Install only Microsoft.Graph.Authentication and Microsoft.Graph.Users, then run Connect-MgGraph -Scopes User.Read.All and Get-MgUser against a test tenant.
microsoftgraph/msgraph-sdk-powershell.why: Official PowerShell modules for Microsoft Graph, used to script Entra ID users and groups, Intune devices, Exchange/Teams data and compliance tasks across Microsoft 365.

mthcht/awesome-lists.first_step: Download one list, such as the RMM or suspicious OAuth app IDs CSV, and run it as a read-only lookup against existing SIEM or Entra sign-in logs to review the hits.
mthcht/awesome-lists.why: Auto-updated detection lists (suspicious TLDs, ASNs, VPN/Tor IPs, RMM tools, LOLDrivers, OAuth app IDs, Entra/AD privileged roles) for feeding SIEM lookups, firewall blocklists and conditional access rules.

mukul975/cve-mcp-server.first_step: Run it locally with Claude Desktop using only the free no-key tools, and triage a few known CVEs from your current patch backlog.
mukul975/cve-mcp-server.why: MCP server that lets Claude triage CVEs by pulling NVD, EPSS, CISA KEV, and threat-intel lookups (VirusTotal, Shodan), which helps patch prioritization and vulnerability review.

munki/munki.first_step: Install a release package on a test Mac and point it at a small local repo with one app to verify the install and removal workflow.
munki/munki.why: Munki manages software installs, removals and Apple update prompts on Mac fleets from a web-hosted package repository. It is widely paired with Jamf or Intune for app deployment.

nautobot/nautobot.first_step: Explore demo.nautobot.com, then stand up a local Docker instance and import a small sample of sites, prefixes and devices before connecting any live gear.
nautobot/nautobot.why: Network source of truth (IPAM, DCIM, VLANs, circuits) with a jobs engine for config backup, golden config compliance and device onboarding. Most useful to teams managing sizable network fleets.

netalertx/netalertx.first_step: Run the Docker container on a single lab or office VLAN with notifications off, and compare the devices it discovers against your existing inventory.
netalertx/netalertx.why: Self-hosted network device discovery via arp-scan, DHCP, UniFi and SNMP imports, with alerts on new or unauthorized devices. Useful for spotting shadow IT and keeping a rough asset inventory across sites.

netbirdio/netbird.first_step: Deploy the self-hosted quickstart on a test VM with a sandbox IdP, enroll two non-production machines, and test access policies before touching production.
netbirdio/netbird.why: Self-hostable WireGuard mesh VPN/ZTNA with IdP SSO, group sync, posture checks and access policies. A candidate to replace a legacy VPN for remote access to internal resources.

netbox-community/devicetype-library.first_step: Use the Device-Type-Library-Import script to load a single vendor's definitions into a test NetBox instance and check them for duplicates before importing to production.
netbox-community/devicetype-library.why: Community YAML library of device and module type definitions for NetBox, so you can populate racks and inventory without hand-entering switch, server and PDU specs.

netbox-community/netbox.first_step: Explore the public demo at demo.netbox.dev, then deploy the community Docker image in a lab and import a small subnet and rack inventory.
netbox-community/netbox.why: NetBox is a source of truth for IPAM and DCIM. It documents racks, devices, cables, IPs, VLANs and circuits, and exposes REST APIs that feed Ansible, monitoring and config rendering.

netbox-community/netbox-docker.first_step: Clone the release branch and run docker compose up on a lab host to evaluate NetBox with sample data before planning a production deployment.
netbox-community/netbox-docker.why: Official community Docker Compose packaging for NetBox, the network source of truth and DCIM/IPAM tool. It makes deploying and upgrading a NetBox instance for tracking racks, IPs, and devices straightforward.

netbox-community/netbox-topology-views.first_step: Install the version matching your NetBox release in a test or staging NetBox instance and generate a topology view for one site.
netbox-community/netbox-topology-views.why: NetBox plugin that draws network topology maps from cabled devices, filterable by site, tag and role, with export to draw.io XML or PNG for network documentation.

netbox-community/pynetbox.first_step: Install with pip and run read-only queries like nb.dcim.devices.all() against a test NetBox instance using a read-only token with strict_filters=True.
netbox-community/pynetbox.why: Python client for the NetBox API, used to script queries and updates to a network source of truth (devices, IPs, sites) for inventory sync and automation.

normation/rudder.first_step: Browse the public demo UI, then install Rudder Core on a lab VM with one test Linux agent in audit (check-only) mode.
normation/rudder.why: Configuration management and compliance platform for Linux servers (Windows requires a paid plan), covering inventory, patching, hardening and continuous policy enforcement. It is server-infrastructure focused rather than tied to MDM or SaaS stacks.

nozaq/terraform-aws-secure-baseline.first_step: Run terraform plan with the module against a sandbox AWS account and review the planned changes before applying, especially the default VPC rule removal.
nozaq/terraform-aws-secure-baseline.why: Terraform module that applies CIS and AWS FSBP baseline controls to AWS accounts: CloudTrail, Config, GuardDuty, SecurityHub, IAM password policy, and default VPC lockdown. Useful for IT teams that own AWS accounts.

oauth2-proxy/oauth2-proxy.first_step: Deploy the container in front of a non-critical internal test app using a dedicated test OIDC app registration in your Entra ID or Okta tenant.
oauth2-proxy/oauth2-proxy.why: Puts SSO (Entra ID, Google, generic OIDC) in front of internal web apps that lack native auth, forwarding user and group headers upstream.

okta/okta-sdk-python.first_step: Create an OAuth service app in an Okta developer org with only the okta.users.read scope and run a list_users script.
okta/okta-sdk-python.why: Official Python SDK for the Okta Management API, used to script user lifecycle, group membership, and app assignment tasks. It is a building block, so you write your own automation on top of it.

okta/terraform-provider-okta.first_step: Pin v6.15.0 and run terraform plan with data sources and import blocks against an Okta preview/sandbox org to codify existing config without making changes.
okta/terraform-provider-okta.why: Official Okta-maintained Terraform provider for managing Okta users, groups, apps, and policies as code, letting you version-control and review identity configuration changes.

olivetin/olivetin.first_step: Run the container locally with a YAML config containing one harmless read-only command (e.g. uptime or df -h) and review its auth and logging before exposing real scripts.
olivetin/olivetin.why: Self-hosted web UI that exposes predefined shell commands as buttons and forms, letting helpdesk or junior admins run vetted scripts (restarts, backups) with logging of who ran what.

open-policy-agent/opa.first_step: Run the OPA CLI locally and evaluate a sample Rego policy against exported JSON, such as a Terraform plan, in the Rego Playground or with opa eval.
open-policy-agent/opa.why: General-purpose policy engine (Rego) for authorization and compliance checks across Kubernetes, Terraform, Docker and SSH/sudo. Mostly a platform/DevOps building block; it does not directly cover mainstream IT admin stacks.

opsmill/infrahub.first_step: Explore the hosted sandbox or run the local quick start with sample data before importing any real inventory.
opsmill/infrahub.why: Network source-of-truth platform (IPAM, DCIM, devices, VLANs) with versioned data and config generation, integrating with Ansible, Nornir and NetBox sync for infrastructure automation.

orange-cyberdefense/goad.first_step: Deploy GOAD-Light or MINILAB on an isolated hypervisor host with no internet exposure to test AD attack detection and hardening changes.
orange-cyberdefense/goad.why: Builds an intentionally vulnerable Active Directory lab (multi-forest, SCCM) for practicing attack techniques. Useful for testing AD detections and hardening, not for production admin.

outflanknl/redelk.first_step: If your org runs red team exercises, deploy it in an isolated lab with the Docker images and the wiki guide, then review its redirector-traffic queries for detection ideas.
outflanknl/redelk.why: A red team SIEM built on ELK that collects C2 teamserver and redirector logs and flags when defenders investigate the infrastructure. It is mainly useful to internal red teams, not to day-to-day IT administration.

owasp/nettacker.first_step: Run the Docker image with only the port_scan module against a small lab subnet you own, with written authorization, and review the HTML report before enabling any brute-force modules.
owasp/nettacker.why: Scans IP ranges and domains for open ports, services, default credentials and known CVEs, and keeps scan history so new or changed hosts show up between runs. Useful for internal exposure checks and shadow IT discovery.

pablosnt/rekono.first_step: Deploy with docker compose in a lab, change the default rekono:rekono password, and run a low-aggressiveness scan against a single host you own and are authorized to test.
pablosnt/rekono.why: Self-hosted platform that chains Nmap, Nuclei, SSL and web scanners to map your external attack surface and track vulnerabilities over time. Useful for recurring exposure checks of your own perimeter.

patchmon/patchmon.first_step: Deploy the Docker stack in a lab, enroll one or two non-production Linux hosts, and review inventory and dry-run results before approving any patch runs.
patchmon/patchmon.why: Self-hosted Linux/FreeBSD/Windows server patch management with package inventory, dry-run and approved patch runs, scheduling, CIS/OpenSCAP compliance scans and OIDC SSO.

pegaprox/project-pegaprox.first_step: Deploy it on a test VM, connect a lab Proxmox cluster using a Viewer-role or read-only API account, and review the dashboard and monitoring before enabling any write actions.
pegaprox/project-pegaprox.why: Web console for managing multiple Proxmox VE and XCP-ng clusters: VM lifecycle, backups, migrations (including from ESXi), HA, RBAC with LDAP/OIDC, and CVE/CIS checks. Useful where Proxmox is the hypervisor.

pennyw0rth/netexec.first_step: With written authorization, install via pipx in an isolated lab domain and run read-only SMB/LDAP enumeration against test hosts before any production use.
pennyw0rth/netexec.why: Pentest tool (successor to CrackMapExec) for auditing Active Directory and Windows networks over SMB, LDAP, WinRM and similar protocols, e.g. finding weak credentials, open shares and misconfigurations.

pester/pester.first_step: Install the module from PowerShell Gallery in CurrentUser scope and write a few mocked tests for an existing admin script, so it runs without touching real systems.
pester/pester.why: Test and mock framework for PowerShell, used to validate admin scripts and modules before running them against production, and to write infrastructure state checks such as config or file presence tests.

pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-ai.first_step: Deploy it in a lab VM and connect one low-sensitivity test source with a read-only service account, then check that search results respect each user's permissions.
pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-ai.why: Self-hosted enterprise search over Slack, Drive, Microsoft 365, Jira and Confluence with permission-aware results and an MCP server. IT might run it as a knowledge platform, but it does not administer those systems.

pnp/cli-microsoft365.first_step: Install via npm or Docker, run `m365 setup` to register a dedicated Entra app with minimal read permissions in a test tenant, then try list/get commands such as `m365 spo site list`.
pnp/cli-microsoft365.why: Cross-platform CLI for administering a Microsoft 365 tenant (SharePoint Online, Teams, Entra ID, OneDrive, Power Platform, Purview) from bash or PowerShell, with JSON output and JMESPath queries for scripting.

pnp/list-formatting.first_step: Pick a column format from the gallery and apply it to a column in a test list on a non-production SharePoint site, keeping the previous format so you can restore it.
pnp/list-formatting.why: Copy-ready JSON samples for formatting SharePoint and Microsoft Lists columns, views and forms; useful when building IT trackers or request lists in SharePoint, but it is site customization rather than tenant administration.

pnp/powershell.first_step: Install PnP.PowerShell in PowerShell 7.4+, register your own Entra app, and run read-only Get- cmdlets such as Get-PnPTenantSite against a test tenant.
pnp/powershell.why: Widely used PowerShell module with 900+ cmdlets for administering SharePoint Online, Teams and other Microsoft 365 workloads, e.g. site provisioning, permissions reports and bulk changes.

pocket-id/pocket-id.first_step: Deploy it via Docker in a lab, then connect one non-critical internal app as an OIDC client to test passkey sign-in.
pocket-id/pocket-id.why: Self-hosted OIDC/OAuth 2.0 provider with passkey-only sign-in, useful for adding SSO and phishing-resistant MFA to internal or self-hosted apps without the complexity of Keycloak.

powershell/psresourceget.first_step: On a test workstation, run Find-PSResource and Install-PSResource -Scope CurrentUser for a known module such as Microsoft.Graph to compare its behavior with PowerShellGet v2.
powershell/psresourceget.why: Official PowerShell module manager for installing, updating and publishing modules and scripts, including from private repositories, so admins can distribute and version the PowerShell tooling they run against Entra, Intune and M365.

powershellorg/plaster.first_step: Install from the PowerShell Gallery with -Scope CurrentUser and generate a throwaway module from the built-in NewPowerShellScriptModule template in a scratch folder.
powershellorg/plaster.why: Scaffolds PowerShell module projects, Pester tests and DSC configurations from templates, which helps IT teams standardize the layout of their internal automation modules.

powershellorg/pskoans.first_step: Install the module with Install-Module PSKoans -Scope CurrentUser on a workstation, then run Show-Karma to work through the introductory koans.
powershellorg/pskoans.why: Interactive Pester-based exercises for learning PowerShell. Useful for training helpdesk staff or junior admins in the scripting skills behind IT automation, but it doesn't automate any admin task itself.

pranshuparmar/witr.first_step: Install it via brew or winget on a test machine and run `witr --port <port> --json` against a known service to check the output before using it on production hosts.
pranshuparmar/witr.why: CLI/TUI that traces a process, port, container or file back to the service, supervisor or shell that started it on Linux, macOS, Windows and FreeBSD. Useful for troubleshooting servers and endpoints and for incident triage.

project-copacetic/copacetic.first_step: Scan a non-production test image with Trivy, then run copa against that report and push the result to a local registry tag to compare before and after.
project-copacetic/copacetic.why: Patches OS-package vulnerabilities in existing container images using Trivy scan reports, without a full rebuild. Useful for teams that run third-party container workloads and have security SLAs to meet.

prowler-cloud/prowler.first_step: Install via pip and run `prowler azure` or `prowler m365` with a read-only (Reader/SecurityAudit) identity against a test subscription or tenant, then review the report.
prowler-cloud/prowler.why: Runs CIS/NIST/SOC2-style security and compliance checks against AWS, Azure, GCP and (per its docs) Microsoft 365 and other providers, producing compliance evidence and misconfiguration findings.

psake/psake.first_step: Install it from the PowerShell Gallery with -Scope CurrentUser and run one of the example psakefiles locally to see how tasks and dependencies work.
psake/psake.why: PowerShell task runner for build scripts. It is useful for sysadmins who package and test their own PowerShell modules or want dependency-ordered task scripts, but it does not touch IT platforms directly.

psappdeploytoolkit/psappdeploytoolkit.first_step: Install the module from the PowerShell Gallery, generate a template with New-ADTTemplate, and package one simple app to test on a single test VM before deploying it through Intune.
psappdeploytoolkit/psappdeploytoolkit.why: PowerShell framework for packaging and deploying Windows apps through Intune, ConfigMgr or Tanium, with standard install/uninstall workflows, user prompts, deferrals and logging.

psmux/psmux.first_step: Install it via winget on a personal workstation and try a named session with split panes before using it on any admin jump box.
psmux/psmux.why: Native tmux-style terminal multiplexer for Windows, useful for keeping persistent multi-pane PowerShell sessions during remote admin work over SSH. It does not manage any IT platform itself.

pythops/oryx.first_step: Install the binary on a non-production Linux VM with kernel 6.10+ and run 'sudo oryx' to observe traffic without enabling any firewall rules.
pythops/oryx.why: Terminal UI for live packet inspection on Linux hosts using eBPF, with traffic stats and basic firewall rules. Useful for troubleshooting network issues on Linux servers.

rackulalives/rackula.first_step: Try the hosted demo at count.racku.la or run the Docker container locally to map one existing rack.
rackulalives/rackula.why: Drag-and-drop rack elevation designer using NetBox device images, for planning and documenting server/network racks and exporting diagrams for change requests.

rana-gmbh/netfluss.first_step: Install it on one test Mac, leave the privileged helper and DNS rules off, and use it to check per-app bandwidth during a slow-network ticket.
rana-gmbh/netfluss.why: Menubar app for macOS and Windows that shows per-app bandwidth, router traffic (UniFi, OpenWrt, Fritz!Box), DNS switching and VPN status. It is useful for ad-hoc troubleshooting on a single machine, but it is not a fleet admin tool.

raphire/win11debloat.first_step: Run it with command-line parameters on a disposable Windows VM snapshot to see which changes it applies before using it in any image or Intune deployment.
raphire/win11debloat.why: PowerShell script to strip preinstalled apps, disable telemetry/Copilot and set UI defaults on Windows 10/11, with CLI params, audit-mode support and exportable settings for image prep.

reconmap/reconmap.first_step: Run it locally with docker compose and scan only a lab host you own using the built-in Nmap and testssl parsers, with a local Ollama model.
reconmap/reconmap.why: Pentest engagement management platform that runs scanners like Nmap and testssl, parses their output into findings and writes reports. It is aimed at infosec and MSSP teams more than day-to-day IT admin work.

rmbolger/posh-acme.first_step: Install from the PowerShell Gallery for the current user and request a test certificate against the Let's Encrypt staging server, using the Manual DNS plugin on a non-production domain.
rmbolger/posh-acme.why: PowerShell ACME client for issuing and renewing Let's Encrypt or other ACME certificates, with DNS plugins for wildcard certs. Automates the recurring TLS certificate renewal chore on Windows and cross-platform.

romanitho/winget-autoupdate.first_step: Install WAU.msi on a test Windows VM with an included_apps.txt allowlist of a few apps and RUN_WAU=YES, then review the logs before deploying via Intune or GPO.
romanitho/winget-autoupdate.why: Keeps Windows third-party apps patched via winget in system and user context, with allow/block lists, GPO support and Intune log integration for fleet deployment.

rubysec/bundler-audit.first_step: Run `bundle-audit check --update --format json` against the Gemfile.lock of an internal Ruby app you host and review the findings.
rubysec/bundler-audit.why: Developer tool that checks Ruby Gemfile.lock files for gems with known vulnerabilities. Useful to sysadmins only if they run or maintain Ruby apps such as internal Rails tools.

ruudmens/lazyadmin.first_step: Browse the repo for a reporting script (e.g., an AD or M365 user report), read the code and the matching blog guide, then run it in a test environment with read-only permissions.
ruudmens/lazyadmin.why: Collection of PowerShell sysadmin scripts from LazyAdmin.nl, commonly covering AD, Microsoft 365 and Exchange reporting tasks; the README doesn't list specific scripts, so check the repo for coverage.

s1ckb0y1337/active-directory-exploitatio.first_step: Review enumeration techniques and run read-only checks (BloodHound/PowerView collection) against a lab AD to find exposures.
s1ckb0y1337/active-directory-exploitatio.why: AD attack/enumeration cheat sheet useful for sysadmins to understand and test their own Active Directory for Kerberoasting, delegation abuse, ACL weaknesses, and hardening priorities.

safe3/openresty-manager.first_step: Deploy the Docker version on an isolated lab VM, change the default admin password immediately, and test proxying one internal site with a staging certificate.
safe3/openresty-manager.why: Web panel for managing OpenResty reverse proxies, Let's Encrypt certificate renewal, access control and HTTP flood protection, plus host terminal and Docker app management. Useful for self-hosted web services, not core identity/endpoint work.

sebadob/rauthy.first_step: Run the single-instance Docker image with embedded Hiqlite in a lab, then connect one test OIDC app and one test Linux host via PAM.
sebadob/rauthy.why: Self-hosted OIDC/OAuth2 identity provider with passkey MFA, SCIM, audit events, and a PAM module for Linux host logins. A lightweight Keycloak alternative for SSO on internal apps and servers.

sharepoint/sp-dev-docs.first_step: Read the site templates/site scripts and list formatting articles on Microsoft Learn and test examples in a dev tenant.
sharepoint/sp-dev-docs.why: Source for Microsoft's SharePoint developer docs (SPFx, site scripts, list formatting). Mostly developer-focused, but site templates and column formatting docs help SharePoint admins.

sherifabdlnaby/elastdocker.first_step: Deploy it on an isolated lab VM, change the default elastic password in .env, and ingest local Docker logs to evaluate before pointing real log sources at it.
sherifabdlnaby/elastdocker.why: Docker Compose deployment of Elastic Stack with security, monitoring and SIEM preconfigured, for standing up a small log aggregation and SIEM instance for infrastructure logs.

sierrasoftworks/tailscale-unifi.first_step: On a non-production UniFi gateway, review install.sh before running it, then bring up Tailscale without advertised routes and check the result with tailscale status.
sierrasoftworks/tailscale-unifi.why: Installs and maintains Tailscale as a persistent systemd service on UniFi Cloud Gateways, so the gateway can act as a subnet router or exit node for remote access to the site LAN.

silverhack/monkey365.first_step: Install from PowerShell Gallery and run Invoke-Monkey365 with a least-privilege read-only account against a test tenant, exporting to HTML to review findings.
silverhack/monkey365.why: Read-only PowerShell assessment of Microsoft 365, Entra ID and Azure configuration against CIS benchmarks, producing HTML/JSON/CSV findings with remediation guidance for posture reviews and audit evidence.

sirkirby/unifi-mcp.first_step: Install unifi-network-mcp locally over stdio against a lab or non-production controller using a limited local admin account, and only call read/list tools first.
sirkirby/unifi-mcp.why: MCP servers that let AI agents query and manage UniFi Network, Protect and Access controllers: clients, devices, firewall rules, cameras and door access. Useful for UniFi shops; a narrower stack than the mainstream platforms.

skiptotheendpoint/openintunebaseline.first_step: Import the Windows baseline into a test tenant with IntuneManagement or OIB Deployer, assign it only to a pilot device group, and review each setting against your own requirements.
skiptotheendpoint/openintunebaseline.why: Ready-made Intune security baseline policies for Windows, Windows 365 and macOS, mapped to CIS, NCSC and Essential Eight, for hardening managed devices without building every policy by hand.

snailsploit/claude-red.first_step: Review a SKILL.md in an isolated environment to understand attack techniques relevant to your stack, for authorized testing only.
snailsploit/claude-red.why: Offensive security skill library for Claude; useful for red teamers but only adjacent to defensive sysadmin work. Could inform hardening priorities but is not a mainstream admin task tool.

softeria/ms-365-mcp-server.first_step: Run it with --read-only and --list-permissions against a test tenant, then connect it in Claude Desktop with a narrow --preset and --allowed-scopes.
softeria/ms-365-mcp-server.why: MCP server exposing 300+ Microsoft Graph tools (mail, Teams, SharePoint, users) so an agent can query and manage Microsoft 365 tenants, with scope allowlists and tool filtering.

srl-labs/containerlab.first_step: Install containerlab on a Linux VM and deploy a small sample topology using free images such as SR Linux or FRR, then destroy it.
srl-labs/containerlab.why: Builds container-based network labs (Arista, Cisco, Juniper, Fortigate, Palo Alto, etc.) from declarative topology files, so network changes and automation can be tested before they reach production.

stackql/stackql.first_step: Install the CLI and run SELECT queries against the Okta or Azure provider with a read-only API token in a test tenant before trying any provisioning statements.
stackql/stackql.why: Query Okta, Azure, Google, GitHub and other cloud/SaaS APIs with SQL, useful for inventory, access audits and config reporting across tenants; also exposes an MCP server for agents.

stevegilham/altcover.first_step: Not applicable for IT admin work; developers could try the dotnet global tool on a test project.
stevegilham/altcover.why: A .NET code coverage instrumentation tool for developers running tests; it does not address identity, endpoint, SaaS, or other IT administration tasks.

swiftdialog/swiftdialog.first_step: Install the signed pkg on a test Mac and run a simple dialog command with --title and --message from a script to see output and return codes.
swiftdialog/swiftdialog.why: Widely used Mac admin utility for showing user dialogs, onboarding progress screens, update prompts and input forms from Jamf/Intune scripts.

t0pcyber/hawk.first_step: Install from the PowerShell Gallery and run Start-HawkUserInvestigation against a test user in a non-production tenant with read-only audit permissions, noting that the module sends usage telemetry.
t0pcyber/hawk.why: PowerShell module that collects M365 and Entra ID forensic data (audit logs, inbox rules, forwarding, app consents, sign-ins) for compromised-account and tenant incident investigations.

tailscale/tailscale.first_step: Install the packaged client on a couple of test machines joined to a trial tailnet and evaluate ACLs and SSO login before any wider rollout.
tailscale/tailscale.why: Source for the Tailscale client daemon and CLI, used to build mesh VPN access to internal hosts with SSO-backed identity. Useful for remote access setups, though most admins deploy the packaged builds.

tenzir/tenzir.first_step: Run a local Tenzir node in a lab and build a pipeline that reads a sample Zeek or Suricata log file and writes normalized output to a file, before connecting it to any production SIEM.
tenzir/tenzir.why: Pipeline engine for collecting, parsing, normalizing and routing security telemetry (Zeek, Suricata, NetFlow, PCAP) to a SIEM, and for cutting log volume before ingest. Most relevant for teams running their own SOC data flows.

terraform-aws-modules/terraform-aws-iam.first_step: Run terraform plan with the iam-account or SAML role module against a sandbox AWS account and review the proposed changes before applying.
terraform-aws-modules/terraform-aws-iam.why: Terraform modules for managing AWS IAM users, groups, roles, password policy, and SAML/OIDC trust roles for IdPs like Okta. Useful for IT teams that own AWS account access as code.

the-art-of-hacking/h4cker.first_step: Browse the defensive-security and incident-response directories for checklists and references relevant to your environment.
the-art-of-hacking/h4cker.why: A large curated collection of offensive and defensive security references, labs, and cheat sheets. It is useful for security training and DFIR reference, but it does not automate any admin task.

the-viper-one/psmapexec.first_step: Run in an isolated lab AD environment with explicit authorization to understand attack paths against your own setup.
the-viper-one/psmapexec.why: Offensive post-exploitation framework for Active Directory, useful for red-team testing but not a routine admin task. Could inform defensive hardening.

threathunters-io/laurel.first_step: Install LAUREL as an audispd plugin on one non-production Linux host, then check its JSON output before forwarding it to your SIEM.
threathunters-io/laurel.why: An auditd plugin that turns raw Linux audit events into enriched JSON with decoded arguments and parent-process context, so they are easier to ship to and search in a SIEM.

timhartmann7/omnyssh.first_step: Install the TUI or desktop build on a workstation, let it read your existing ~/.ssh/config, and browse a lab host's metrics and files without using the one-click key setup, which disables password login on the server with no confirmation step.
timhartmann7/omnyssh.why: SSH client and server manager with a live host metrics dashboard, SFTP, and parameterized snippets that run on many Linux servers at once. Useful for admins who manage a fleet of Linux boxes or appliances.
