tngan/samlify.first_step: Run the samlify-starter example locally against a test SAML app in a sandbox Okta or Entra tenant, with schema validation enabled.
tngan/samlify.why: Node.js library for building SAML service providers or identity providers. Useful if you write internal apps that need to SSO against Okta or Entra ID, but it is a developer building block, not an admin tool.

tonyphipps/siem.first_step: Read the Microsoft 365 auditing and Windows logging guides and compare their recommended audit settings against your current tenant and GPO configuration.
tonyphipps/siem.why: Documentation collection for SIEM teams: logging and event ID references, hardening guides for Microsoft 365, Entra ID (Azure AD), AD and Windows, plus IR templates and lookup tables for enrichment.

topscoder/nuclei-wordfence-cve.first_step: Install the templates and run nuclei with -tags production -severity critical against a staging copy of a WordPress site you are authorized to scan.
topscoder/nuclei-wordfence-cve.why: Nuclei templates generated from Wordfence intel for scanning WordPress core, plugins and themes for known CVEs. Useful for vulnerability checks on WordPress sites you own, a narrow stack.

turbot/tailpipe.first_step: Install it locally, point the AWS plugin at a copy of CloudTrail logs using a read-only profile, and run the prebuilt detection mod.
turbot/tailpipe.why: Local SQL-based log analysis for cloud logs such as AWS CloudTrail and Azure activity, with prebuilt MITRE-aligned detections. It is useful for incident response and log review, but it is cloud-infra focused rather than identity or endpoint focused.

turroks/cve_prioritizer.first_step: Install via pip and run it against a single known CVE, then against an exported Nessus report from a recent scan, using a free NVD API key.
turroks/cve_prioritizer.why: CLI that ranks CVEs from a list or Nessus/OpenVAS report by CVSS, EPSS and CISA KEV status, helping decide which patches to deploy first.

ucs-care-group/mailcraft.first_step: Install it on a test machine and sign in with a test Microsoft 365 mailbox. Use Outlook alongside it and review which Graph consent scopes it requests before allowing any admin approval.
ucs-care-group/mailcraft.why: An alpha Rust mail/calendar client for Microsoft 365 and IMAP that includes an MCP server and a command channel. It is an end-user client, not an admin tool, so its IT use is limited to scripted mailbox actions.

unpoller/unpoller.first_step: Run the Docker image in Prometheus mode against the UniFi controller using a dedicated read-only controller account, then import one of the provided Grafana dashboards.
unpoller/unpoller.why: Polls a UniFi controller and exports device, client, site, event and IDS data to InfluxDB, Prometheus or Loki, with prebuilt Grafana dashboards for network monitoring. Useful for UniFi shops only.

useopendesk/opendesk.first_step: Run the installer with --dry-run, then deploy it on a test Linux VM with Docker and route a test IT support mailbox into it.
useopendesk/opendesk.why: Self-hostable shared support inbox with ticketing, SLAs, a knowledge base and live chat. It could serve as an internal IT helpdesk, though it is built mainly for customer support rather than ITSM or asset management.

utmstack/utmstack.first_step: Install it on an isolated Ubuntu 22.04 VM, lock down ports to admin workstations, and onboard a few non-production log sources to evaluate detections.
utmstack/utmstack.why: Self-hosted open-source SIEM/XDR that centralizes log collection, correlation, alerting and compliance reporting (HIPAA, SOC 2, CMMC) for servers, endpoints and SaaS sources.

vgrem/office365-rest-python-client.first_step: Register an app with read-only Graph permissions (e.g. User.Read.All, Sites.Read.All) in a test tenant and run one of the example scripts that lists users or SharePoint sites.
vgrem/office365-rest-python-client.why: Python SDK for SharePoint REST and Microsoft Graph that lets you script M365 admin tasks such as SharePoint site and permission reports, OneDrive files, Teams, and Entra ID users and groups.

vibber-ai/fastapi-azure-auth.first_step: Register a test app in a sandbox Entra tenant and protect a demo FastAPI endpoint following the single-tenant tutorial in the docs.
vibber-ai/fastapi-azure-auth.why: Python library for adding Entra ID token validation to FastAPI apps. Useful if you build internal IT tools or APIs that need Entra SSO and role or scope checks, but it is a developer building block rather than an admin tool.

victoriametrics/victorialogs.first_step: Run the single-node Docker image in a lab, forward a test host's syslog to it, and query the logs through the built-in web UI.
victoriametrics/victorialogs.why: Self-hosted log database for centralizing syslog, application and infrastructure logs, with a Grafana plugin; usable as a lightweight alternative to Elasticsearch or Loki for log retention and searching.

voltiusapp/voltius.first_step: Install the desktop client, import an existing PuTTY or Termius host list, and leave the MCP server disabled until you have reviewed which of its tools can execute commands.
voltiusapp/voltius.why: SSH/SFTP/serial client with shared team vaults, imports from PuTTY/MobaXterm/SecureCRT, and an optional MCP server that lets agents run commands on managed hosts. Useful for daily server and network-device access.

wazuh/wazuh.first_step: Deploy the Wazuh Docker stack in a lab and enroll a couple of test endpoints to review vulnerability and configuration-assessment findings before enabling any active responses.
wazuh/wazuh.why: Open-source SIEM/XDR that collects endpoint and syslog data and adds file integrity monitoring, CVE-based vulnerability detection and configuration assessment against hardening baselines such as PCI DSS.

willswire/unifi-ddns.first_step: Deploy the Worker with an API token scoped to a single test zone and point a UniFi custom DDNS entry at a throwaway subdomain.
willswire/unifi-ddns.why: Lets UniFi gateways update Cloudflare DNS A/AAAA records via a Worker, covering multi-hostname and dual-stack DDNS for sites with dynamic WAN IPs.

windshiftapp/core.first_step: Run the Docker image with embedded SQLite on a test host, import a sample Jira project, and evaluate the service portal and asset register before connecting SSO or the MCP server.
windshiftapp/core.why: Self-hosted Jira/JSM alternative with service desk queues, SLAs, request portal, knowledge base and asset/CMDB register; could host IT ticketing and asset tracking with LDAP/OIDC SSO.

xtls/xray-core.first_step: Read the docs at xtls.github.io and run the official Docker image in an isolated lab to see how its traffic appears to your firewall or IDS.
xtls/xray-core.why: A proxy/tunnel core (VLESS, Trojan, Shadowsocks, WireGuard) built for censorship circumvention. It is mainly relevant to sysadmins who need to understand or detect these tunnels on their networks, not for managing corporate VPNs.

xxh/xxh.first_step: Install via pipx and run 'xxh <testhost> +s bash' against a non-production Linux box, then remove ~/.xxh afterward.
xxh/xxh.why: Carries your local shell (zsh, fish, xonsh, bash) and dotfiles to remote Linux hosts over SSH without root. It is a convenience for admins working on Linux servers, and it does not automate any admin task.

yuezk/globalprotect-openconnect.first_step: Install it on a test Linux machine and run `gpclient connect <portal> --browser` against your GlobalProtect portal to confirm SAML login and HIP checks work before recommending it to users.
yuezk/globalprotect-openconnect.why: Third-party GlobalProtect VPN client for Linux/BSD/macOS with SAML SSO, MFA, and HIP reports. Useful for supporting Linux users on a Palo Alto VPN that has no official client option.

zammad/zammad.first_step: Deploy the official docker-compose stack in a test VM and route a test mailbox into it to evaluate the ticket workflow.
zammad/zammad.why: Self-hostable open-source ticketing system for running an IT helpdesk queue across email, chat and phone, with a REST API for integrations. It is customer-support oriented rather than a full ITSM.

zinggai/zingg.first_step: Run the Docker image against the bundled Febrl example, then try a CSV export of duplicate asset or user records.
zinggai/zingg.why: Spark-based ML entity resolution for customer/master data. It is a data engineering tool, though it could help dedupe messy asset or user records merged from multiple HR/IT systems.

zitadel/zitadel.first_step: Deploy the Docker Compose stack in a lab, connect one test app via OIDC or SAML, and review the audit event stream before planning any production use.
zitadel/zitadel.why: Self-hostable IdP providing SSO (OIDC/SAML), MFA, passkeys, SCIM and LDAP federation. Mainly for app developers and B2B platforms, but usable as an internal IdP alternative to Keycloak or Okta.

znuny/znuny.first_step: Deploy the latest release on a test Linux VM with MariaDB or PostgreSQL and walk through a sample ticket workflow before considering any migration.
znuny/znuny.why: Self-hosted open-source ticketing/ITSM system (OTRS Community Edition fork) for running an IT helpdesk queue; a replacement option for teams leaving OTRS CE.

zoicware/removewindowsai.first_step: Download the script, review it, and run it with -backupMode on a snapshot-enabled Windows 11 test VM before considering selected options for deployment.
zoicware/removewindowsai.why: PowerShell script that disables and removes Windows 11 AI features (Copilot, Recall, AI appx/CBS packages) via registry, policy and package removal. It is usable for fleet hardening, but it is aggressive and consumer-oriented compared with managing these features through Intune or GPO.
